title: Consumer-driven timeout synthesis and keepalive recipes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: SDK consumers (Python/TS/Go) are seeing inconsistent error modes when inference requests span short interactive calls and long streaming sessions. Different SDKs ship different transport defaults (socket keepalive, connection pool sizes, per-request deadlines) which causes: silent stream disconnects, noisy retries that harm latency, and poor connection reuse under bursty PLG workloads.

Goal: Produce a cross-SDK guidance + code recipes that let application teams pick safe, production-ready defaults and opt-in autotuning knobs; deliver example configs for Python (requests + httpx/aiohttp), TypeScript (node-agent/fetch), and Go (net/http/Transport). Provide a short compatibility shim pattern for customers who want identical semantics across languages.

Decisions / recommendations so far (consensus at design review 2026-03-02):
- Timeout synthesis: provide two recommended patterns: "interactive" (tight overall deadline) and "streaming" (no global generation timeout; instead use per-chunk idle/read timeout). Default interactive request timeout = 60s, default streaming idle read timeout = 90s. Document strong guidance to avoid bundling both (i.e. do not set a global 60s deadline on a streaming request).
- Keepalive / idle connection policy: default IdleConnTimeout = 90s, TCP keepalive probe = 30s, MaxIdleConnsPerHost = 100 for server-side usage; for single-CPU client libraries recommend scale = max(16, 2 * CPU_count).
- Connection pool sizing: recommend a formula: pooled_conns = min(512, 8 * concurrent_workers). Provide quick heuristics for serverless vs dedicated-hosted.
- Retry window: client-visible retries should be idempotency-aware. For safety, SDKs default to: no automatic write-once retry for streaming; for non-streaming generation: 1 retry for transient 5xx with exponential backoff capped at 2s. Make retry window configurable via RetryPolicy object.
- Backpressure for streaming: expose a consumer-facing FlowControl token bucket (allowing tokens-per-chunk) in SDKs that work with the language runtime (Python asyncio, Node streams, Go channels). Document examples to pause consuming when local processing lag exceeds N ms.

Compatibility recipes (examples included in repo):
- Python (httpx/aiohttp): HTTPX AsyncClient with limits: transport=HTTPTransport(retries=1), limits=Limits(max_keepalive_connections=100, max_connections=200), timeout=Timeout(60.0). For streaming: timeout=None, stream_read_timeout=90.0 (example code in repo).
- TypeScript (node): new Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 256, keepAliveMsecs: 1000 }); axios.create({ httpAgent: agent, timeout: 60000 }); streaming: set timeout: 0 and use per-chunk read watchdog.
- Go: &http.Transport{MaxIdleConns: 512, MaxIdleConnsPerHost: max(32, runtime.NumCPU()*8), IdleConnTimeout: 90*time.Second, TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10*time.Second}; client.Timeout = 60*time.Second for blocking calls; streaming paths use context.WithCancel + idle read timer of 90s.

Telemetry + tests: run synthetic load (1000 concurrent clients, 50 RPS per client) with burst scenarios. Measure: connection reuse ratio, socket churn, P50/P95 latency, stream disconnect rate. Early perf run (2026-03-05) shows IdleConnTimeout=90s reduces socket churn by ~37% and improves P95 by ~12% in our hosted environment.

Deliverables: cross-sdk examples folder, docs page (consumer-timeout-synthesis), unify RetryPolicy shape across SDKs, and integration tests for streaming backpressure.

Open questions / tradeoffs: optimal keepalive probe interval is platform dependent (cloud LB idle timeouts vary). We will ship conservative defaults but add "autotune" helper that reads environment metadata (max CPU, detected cloud idle timeout) to nudge values.
